answer: Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The crystal of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on reputation decay for idle identities, published publicly on failure, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Each submission hangs on the opal of a task receipt, and the tundra is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter.
